explanation:
All 137 FastMath tests pass (1 pre-existing skipped). The refactoring is complete and verified.

## Summary of changes

In `src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math3/util/FastMath.java`, I extracted two helper methods from `reducePayneHanek`, which had clear duplication in its fixed-point multi-precision arithmetic:

**`unsignedMultiply64x64(a, b, c, d, product)`** — performs the unsigned 128-bit product of two 64-bit operands already split into `(high32, low32)` pairs, writing `{high64, low64}` to the output array. This replaces two identical ~26-line blocks (one for input × shpiA, one for prodA × PI_O_4_BITS[0]).

**`accumulateUpperProduct(a, b, c, d, acc)`** — accumulates the upper 64 bits of a partial product into a 128-bit accumulator. This replaces three identical ~15-line blocks (one for shpiB, two for PI_O_4_BITS) where the low 32 bits of the partial product are dropped on purpose.

The remaining shpi0 multiply pattern is structurally different (only adds to the high word) and is used once, so I left it inline but kept a brief comment explaining why. The body of `reducePayneHanek` shrank from ~180 lines of bit-twiddling to a much cleaner sequence of three clearly-named operations: full multiply, accumulate, then convert to double — all without changing any numerical behavior or public API. Cold path (only entered for arguments above π·2²⁰), so the two small `long[2]` allocations are inconsequential.
